issue_context.title: Running ansible-pull in parallel
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
Executing two or more instances of ansible-pull in parallel without specifying the parameter "-d <DEST>, --directory <DEST>" results in undefined behaviour with race conditions.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- ~Bug  Report~
- Docs Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-pull

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```
ansible 2.7.7
  config file = /home/user/.ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/user/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.7.3 (default, Apr  3 2019, 05:39:12) [GCC 8.3.0]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
```
[DEPRECATION WARNING]: DEFAULT_SUDO_FLAGS option, In favor of Ansible Become, which is a generic framework. See become_flags. , use become instead. This feature will be removed in version 2.8. Deprecation 
warnings can be disabled by setting deprecation_warnings=False in ansible.cfg.
ALLOW_WORLD_READABLE_TMPFILES(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = True
ANSIBLE_NOCOWS(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = True
ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = -o ForwardAgent=yes
DEFAULT_FORKS(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = 50
DEFAULT_GATHERING(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = explicit
DEFAULT_HOST_LIST(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = ['/home/user/inventories/common/hosts']
DEFAULT_ROLES_PATH(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = ['/home/user/roles']
DEFAULT_SCP_IF_SSH(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = True
DEFAULT_SUDO_FLAGS(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = -i
DEFAULT_TRANSPORT(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = smart
HOST_KEY_CHECKING(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = True
RETRY_FILES_ENABLED(/home/user/.ansible.cfg) = False
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
debian

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
```
any valid playbook
```

Execute:
```
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository &
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository &
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository &
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository &
```

Related lines of code:

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/pull.py#L124-L131

It would be good to document this as 

https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/cli/ansible-pull.html

does not mention that in any way. It would be wise to introduce some kind of a check to see if the repository present in that folder is the one which is provided and abort in case of a missmatch.

It would be good to create an option to use a temporary folder instead of needing to create one by the calling process. This would eliminate the need to pass both arguments "--clean" and "--purge".

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
All playbooks should be executed.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
Race conditions, different outputs. Here are some examples
```
 [ERROR]: Failed to remove /home/user/.ansible/pull/localhost: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/user/.ansible/pull/localhost'
```

```
localhost | FAILED! => {
    "changed": false,
    "msg": "Unable to determine hashes of submodules",
    "rc": 128,
    "stderr": "fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.\nUse '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:\n'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'\nfatal: run_command returned non-zero status for roles/myrole\n.\n",
    "stderr_lines": [
        "fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.",
        "Use '--' to separate paths from revisions, like this:",
        "'git <command> [<revision>...] -- [<file>...]'",
        "fatal: run_command returned non-zero status for roles/myrole",
        "."
    ],
    "stdout": "Entering 'roles/myrole'\nHEAD\n",
    "stdout_lines": [
        "Entering 'roles/myrole'",
        "HEAD"
    ]
}
```

```
localhost | FAILED! => {
    "changed": false,
    "msg": "Failed to checkout branch master",
    "rc": 1,
    "stderr": "error: pathspec 'master' did not match any file(s) known to git\n",
    "stderr_lines": [
        "error: pathspec 'master' did not match any file(s) known to git"
    ],
    "stdout": "",
    "stdout_lines": []
}
```

Possible Misunderstanding
=========================

Hi!

Thanks very much for your submission to Ansible.  It sincerely means a lot to us.

We believe the ticket you have filed is being somewhat misunderstood, as one thing works a little differently than stated.

The ansible-pull client is not meant to run in parallel on the same host against the same checkout, you should either add a lock (setlock/flock) around the invocation or use separate directories.

In the future, this might be a topic more well suited for the user list, which you can also post here if you'd like some more help with the above.
   
   * https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/ansible-project

Thank you once again for this and your interest in Ansible!

Hi,

Thank you for your response.

As I have mentioned above, I did not see this documented in any way [1], hence my bug report. I had to read through the source code [2] in order to find out what was going on in my particular use case. I later created the simple example above to make a point.

I want to point out, that the above example can also be transformed into:

```
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository1 &
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository2 &
```

I want to also point this example out:

```
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository -e var=1 &
ansible-pull --clean --track-subs --purge --full -U https://myrepository -e var=2 &
```

The implications of running these and other examples (as this is not limited to the "--clean --track-subs --purge --full" options I have provided) should at least, in my opinion, be mentioned in the documentation [1].

The workaround that you have provided should also be mentioned in the documentation [1] as it might be useful to some.

Moreover, an additional option to use a unique empty temporary directory would remove the burden of the caller having to implement some workaround on each call to ansible-pull.

Here is an example of how clean that might look like, if the default behaviour was changed:

```
ansible-pull -U https://myrepository1 &
ansible-pull -U https://myrepository2 &
```

In this example, the application would use a temporary folder for each invocation. The temporary folder would be discarded after the invocation. One might also consider using a locking mechanism as an additional safety measure. A user, who wants to save the checkout and use it later would still be able to do so by providing the "-d" parameter. Other parameters that manipulate the checkout would not be affected by this change as well.

I hope my report helps to make the documentation more clear about the way this tool is supposed to be used as well as its limitations.

Moreover, I hope that I might convince you, to change the behaviour of the application, so that it is more resilient and easy to use.

References:

1: https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/cli/ansible-pull.html
2: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/pull.py#L124-L131
noted, reopening as a docs issue, it should be clear that pull (actually most of ansible CLI tools) are not meant to be run in parallel against the same targets.

Documentation fix:

At line https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blame/devel/docs/docsite/rst/command_guide/command_line_tools.rst#L8 add a note to say -
.. note::
   You should not run most Ansible CLI tools in parallel against the same targets.

And also in the `ansible-pull` file at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/pull.py#L40  add:

 `ansible-pull` is not meant to run in parallel on the same host against the same checkout. You should either add a lock (``setlock/flock``) around the invocation or use separate directories.
Hello @bcoca. Are you still working on this issue or is it available for assignment?

review_comments:
this is very specific to your situation, I would generalize this:

'None of the CLI tools are designed to run concurrently with themselves, you should use an external scheduler and/or locking to ensure there are no clashing operations'

Even running from a different directory might create a concurrency problem with 2 instances trying to modify the same resources.
